newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Fresh Ivorian student strike bites.
newsitem.headline: Fresh Ivorian student strike bites.

text.p: Students in Ivory Coast's universities boycotted classes on Tuesday following a five-day strike call by the Ivorian student federation FESCI, witnesses and college officials said.
The federation, which the government says is banned, called the strike to demand the release of its leaders and other militants detained after campus unrest and talks on other grievances.

Lecturers turned up at the biggest campus in the commercial capital Abidjan but students boycotted classes. A college official in the second city of Bouake said that most students boycotted classes there too.
"Our lecture theatres are overcrowded. No lights, no microphones, and no air conditioning," one student said.

"We are following the call for the five-day strike," another added, but rejected that it was to back FESCI. "This is a way to press for our demands, and to bring government authorities a little closer to the negotiating table."
Student demands include payment of grant arrears and an improvement in housing and studying conditions.
A lecturers' union close to the opposition held a two-day strike in January after the mysterious death of a student after a police raid on a university hall of residence.
Abidjan's Cocody University was built following independence from France in 1960 to accomodate 7,000 students. It now has 50,000.
